newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica fixed investment up in third quarter - bank.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica fixed investment up in third quarter - bank.

text.p: The upward momentum in South African gross domestic fixed investment since the third quarter of 1993 continued in the third quarter of 1996, the Reserve Bank said on Thursday.

In its latest quarterly bulletin, the central bank said current estimates suggested that increases in total real gross domestic fixed investment -- at an annualised rate of eight percent in the first quarter of 1996 and six and a half percent in the second quarter -- were followed by a further rise of three and a half percent in the third quarter.

It said real gross domestic fixed investment in the first three quarters of 1996 was about seven and a half percent higher than in the first three quarters of 1995 compared with growth of ten and a half percent in 1995 as a whole.

"The further improvement in capital formation in the third quarter was brought about by an expansion of real capital expenditure by all three institutional sectors, namely the private sector, public corporations and public authorities," the bank said.

Growth in private sector investment spending increased to an annualised five percent in the first quarter of 1996 and eight percent in the second quarter but then slowed to four percent in the third quarter.
All main production sectors, apart from the mining industry, contributed to the creation of additional production capacity in the third quarter of 1996.
Real fixed capital formation by the public sector increased at an annualised rate of two and a half percent in the third quarter, the bank said.
"The investment activities of public corporations were mostly concentrated in the sectors supplying electricity, gas, water and telecommunications services."

The bank said the gradual reduction in inventory investment since the third quarter of 1995, disrupted by a substantial increase in inventory accumulation in the second quarter of 1996, resumed its downward tend in the third quarter.

"Expressed at constant 1990 prices, inventories increased at an annualised rate of 2.3 billion rand in the first quarter of 1996 and 7.3 billion rand in the second quarter, against only 2.9 billion rand in the third quarter," it said.

Whereas the change in real inventory investment raised the growth of real domestic product by seven percentage points in the second quarter of 1996, it reduced overall growth by six percentage points in the third quarter.

Despite the slower pace of inventory accumulation in the third quarter of 1996, the ratio of industrial and commercial inventories to gross domestic product in the non-agricultural sectors of the economy remained broadly unchanged at the 18 and a half percent level reached in the second quarter, the bank said.
